question.problem: Which integral gives the area of the finite region bounded between $y={x}^{2}-4x+3$ and $y=x-1?$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's draw a sketch of the two functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273827/assets/c286710c66df6613cf448089a76902e63ed4783d31a89c728d5022a382ce3ddf.png)

*(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)*

Now, we want to determine the limits of integration. To do this, we equate the two functions and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-4x+3 & =x-1 \\ {x}^{2}-5x+4 & =0 \\ (x-1)(x-4) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we need to integrate from $x=1$ to $x=4.$

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273827/assets/af15b99ba9e1233c76b6089fb1b4fb6cb62b9edcbedc7f0a241212075be3d33c.png)

The vertical line 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y={x}^{2}-4x+3,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=x-1.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{1}^{4}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}[\,(x-1)-({x}^{2}-4x+3)\,]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}(-{x}^{2}+5x-4)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
